summary: Describes the process for registering new BGP path attribute type codes with IANA. It points to the basic attribute types described in the BGP specification of the time.

plainLanguage.summary: BGP uses numbered codes to identify routing attributes. This memo explains the process it described for requesting a new code.

questions: how to register a bgp attribute type
how to register a bgp attribute code
subtitle: How new BGP attribute type codes were to be documented and assigned.

tldr.problem: BGP attribute type codes need coordinated assignment so that new attributes have documented numeric values.
tldr.mechanism: The memo says new attribute types are documented in an RFC, with octet 255 used during development and IANA assigning the final code.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2042 records an informational registration process and lists the attribute codes then in use.

today: RFC 2042 is Informational. The unit metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC for it.

sections.title: BGP Attribute Type Codes
sections.content:
BGP uses attribute type codes to identify attributes carried with routing information. RFC 2042 says the basic codes were described in RFC 1771 and that codes used on the Internet are registered with IANA.

The memo describes how new attribute codes should be documented and assigned. It does not divide the code space into public, private, IP, or OSI portions.
sections.plainLanguage: Each BGP attribute has a number that identifies it. The memo says those numbers should be documented and registered centrally.

sections.title: Developing and Registering a New Code
sections.content:
While a new attribute type is being developed, the memo reserves octet value 255 for that purpose. When IANA assigns a number, the documentation and code base are updated to use the authorized value.

Requests should go to IANA with “BGP Attribute Type” in the subject. The RFC says IANA-maintained values will appear in the periodically updated Assigned Numbers RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: Use 255 as a temporary development value. Once IANA assigns the official number, update the code and its documentation.

sections.title: Codes Listed in the Memo
sections.content:
The memo lists attribute codes 1 through 13 in use at the time, including ORIGIN, AS_PATH, NEXT_HOP, COMMUNITY, and CLUSTER_LIST. It also lists 255 as reserved for development.

The list reflects this RFC's publication context. The memo does not discuss security issues.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC includes a snapshot of BGP attribute codes then in use. It marks 255 as reserved for development.
